entries.c57e89360a0ac4c4185b59caf89eb79d83409537: <div sID="gen2738" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Num.4" sID="Num.4"/> <div eID="gen2738" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2739" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen2740" type="x-p"/> In the former chapter an account was taken of the whole tribe of Levi, in this we have an account of those of that tribe who were in the prime of their time for service, betwixt thirty and fifty years old. I. The serviceable men of the Kohathites are ordered to be numbered, and their charges are given them, <reference osisRef="Num.4.2-Num.4.20">ver. 2-20</reference>. II. Of the Gershonites, <reference osisRef="Num.4.24-Num.4.28">ver. 24-28</reference>. III. Of the Merarites, <reference osisRef="Num.4.29-Num.4.33">ver. 29-33</reference>. IV. The numbers of each, and the sum total at last, are recorded, <reference osisRef="Num.4.34-Num.4.49">ver. 34</reference>, &c.
entries.518827dcd756d9c6c0b51efed57b3606696a6d47: <div eID="gen2740" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen2739" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Office of the Levites. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1490.)</title> <div sID="gen2741" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, <hi type="super">2</hi> Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, after their families, by the house of their fathers, <hi type="super">3</hi> From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all that enter into the host, to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. <hi type="super">4</hi> This <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the service of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation, <hi type="italic">about</hi> the most holy things: 5 And when the camp setteth forward, Aaron shall come, and his sons, and they shall take down the covering vail, and cover the ark of testimony with it: <hi type="super">6</hi> And shall put thereon the covering of badgers' skins, and shall spread over <hi type="italic">it</hi> a cloth wholly of blue, and shall put in the staves thereof. <hi type="super">7</hi> And upon the table of showbread they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put thereon the dishes, and the spoons, and the bowls, and covers to cover withal: and the continual bread shall be thereon: <hi type="super">8</hi> And they shall spread upon them a cloth of scarlet, and cover the same with a covering of badgers' skins, and shall put in the staves thereof. <hi type="super">9</hi> And they shall take a cloth of blue, and cover the candlestick of the light, and his lamps, and his tongs, and his snuffdishes, and all the oil vessels thereof, wherewith they minister unto it: <hi type="super">10</hi> And they shall put it and all the vessels thereof within a covering of badgers' skins, and shall put <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon a bar. <hi type="super">11</hi> And upon the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue, and cover it with a covering of badgers' skins, and shall put to the staves thereof: <hi type="super">12</hi> And they shall take all the instruments of ministry, wherewith they minister in the sanctuary, and put <hi type="italic">them</hi> in a cloth of blue, and cover them with a covering of badgers' skins, and shall put <hi type="italic">them</hi> on a bar: <hi type="super">13</hi> And they shall take away the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth thereon: <hi type="super">14</hi> And they shall put upon it all the vessels thereof, wherewith they minister about it, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the censers, the fleshhooks, and the shovels, and the basons, all the vessels of the altar; and they shall spread upon it a covering of badgers' skins, and put to the staves of it. <hi type="super">15</hi> And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear <hi type="italic">it:</hi> but they shall not touch <hi type="italic">any</hi> holy thing, lest they die. These <hi type="italic">things are</hi> the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation. 16 And to the office of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest <hi type="italic">pertaineth</hi> the oil for the light, and the sweet incense, and the daily meat offering, and the anointing oil, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the oversight of all the tabernacle, and of all that therein <hi type="italic">is,</hi> in the sanctuary, and in the vessels thereof. <hi type="super">17</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, <hi type="super">18</hi> Cut ye not off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites: <hi type="super">19</hi> But thus do unto them, that they may live, and not die, when they approach unto the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in, and appoint them every one to his service and to his burden: <hi type="super">20</hi> But they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die. <div eID="gen2741" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2742" type="x-p"/> We have here a second muster of the tribe of Levi. As that tribe was taken out of all Israel to be God's peculiar, so the middle-aged men of that tribe were taken from among the rest to be actually employed in the service of the tabernacle. Now observe, <div eID="gen2742" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2743" type="x-p"/> I. Who were to be taken into this number. All the males from thirty years old to fifty. Of the other tribes, those that were numbered to go forth to war were from twenty years old and upward, but of the Levites only from thirty to fifty; for the service of God requires the best of our strength, and the prime of our time, which cannot be better spent than to the honour of him who is the first and best. And a man may make a good soldier much sooner than a good minister. Now, <div eID="gen2743" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2744" type="x-p"/> 1. They were not to be employed till they were thirty years old, because till then they were in danger of retaining something childish and youthful and had not gravity enough to do the service, and wear the honour, of a Levite. They were entered as probationers at twenty-five years old, (<reference osisRef="Num.8.24">ch. viii. 24</reference>), and in David's time, when there was more work to be done, at twenty (<reference osisRef="1Chr.23.24">1 Chron. xxiii. 24</reference>, and so <reference osisRef="Ezra.3.8">Ezra iii. 8</reference>); but they must be five years learning and waiting, and so fitting themselves for service; nay, in David's time they were ten years in preparation, from twenty to thirty. John Baptist began his public ministry, and Christ his, at thirty years old. This is not in the letter of it obligatory on gospel ministers now, as if they must either not begin their work till thirty years old or must leave off at fifty; but it gives us two good rules:—(1.) That ministers must not be novices, <reference osisRef="1Tim.3.6">1 Tim. iii. 6</reference>. It is a work that requires ripeness of judgment and great steadiness, and therefore those are very unfit for it who are but babes in knowledge and have not put away childish things. (2.) That they must learn before they teach, serve before they rule, and must <hi type="italic">first be proved,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Tim.3.10">1 Tim. iii. 10</reference>. <div eID="gen2744" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2745" type="x-p"/> 2. They were discharged at fifty years old from the toilsome part of the service, particularly that of carrying the tabernacle; for that is the special service to which they are here ordained, and which there was most occasion for while they were in the wilderness. When they began to enter upon old age, they were dismissed, (1.) In favour to them, that they might not be over-toiled when their strength began to decay. Twenty years' good service was thought pretty well for one man. (2.) In honour to the work, that it might not be done by those who, through the infirmities of age, were slow and heavy. The service of God should be done when we are in the most lively active frame. Those do not consider this who put off their repentance to old age, and so leave the best work to be done in the worst time. <div eID="gen2745" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2746" type="x-p"/> II. How their work is described. They are said to <hi type="italic">enter into the host,</hi> or warfare, <hi type="italic">to do the work in the tabernacle.</hi> The ministry is <hi type="italic">a good work</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Tim.3.1">1 Tim. iii. 1</reference>): ministers are not ordained to the honour only, but to the labour, not only to have the wages, but to do the work. It is also a <hi type="italic">good warfare,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Tim.1.18">1 Tim. i. 18</reference>. Those that enter into the ministry must look upon themselves as entered into the <hi type="italic">host,</hi> and approve themselves <hi type="italic">good soldiers,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Tim.2.3">2 Tim. ii. 3</reference>. Now, as to the sons of Kohath in particular, here is, <div eID="gen2746" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2747" type="x-p"/> 1. Their service appointed them, in the removes of the tabernacle. Afterwards, when the tabernacle was fixed, they had other work assigned them; but this was the work of the day, which was to be done in its day. Observe, Wherever the camp of Israel went, the tabernacle of the Lord went with them, and care must be taken for the carriage of it. Note, Wherever we go, we must see to it that we take our religion along with us, and not forget that or any part of it. Now the Kohathites were to carry all the holy things of the tabernacle. They were charged with those things before (<reference osisRef="Num.3.31">ch. iii. 31</reference>), but here they have more particular instructions given them. (1.) Aaron, and his sons the priests, must pack up the things which the Kohathites were to carry, as here directed, <reference osisRef="Num.4.5">v. 5</reference>, &c. God had before appointed that none should come into the most holy place, but only Aaron once a year with a cloud of incense (<reference osisRef="Lev.16.2">Lev. xvi. 2</reference>); and yet, the necessity of their unsettled state requiring it, that law is here dispensed with; for every time they removed Aaron and his sons went in to take down the ark, and make it up for carriage; for (as the learned bishop Patrick suggests) the <hi type="italic">shechinah,</hi> or display of the divine majesty, which was over the mercy-seat, removed for the present in the pillar of cloud, which was taken up, and then the ark was not dangerous to be approached. (2.) All the holy things must be covered, the ark and table with three coverings, all the rest with two. Even the ashes of the altar, in which the holy fire was carefully preserved and raked up, must have a purple cloth spread over them, <reference osisRef="Num.4.13">v. 13</reference>. Even the brazen altar, though in the court of the sanctuary it stood open to the view of all, yet was covered in the carriage of it. All these coverings were designed, [1.] For safety, that these holy things might not be ruffled with the wind, sullied with the rain, nor tarnished with the sun, but that they might be preserved in their beauty; for <hi type="italic">on all the glory shall be a defence.</hi> The coverings of badgers' skins, being thick and strong, would keep out wet; and, while we are in our passage through the wilderness of this world, it concerns us to be fenced <hi type="italic">for all weathers,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.4.5-Isa.4.6">Isa. iv. 5, 6</reference>. [2.] For decency and ornament. Most of these things had a cloth of blue, or purple, or scarlet, spread outmost; and the ark was covered with a cloth <hi type="italic">wholly of blue</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.4.6">v. 6</reference>), an emblem (say some) of the azure skies, which are spread like a curtain between us and the Majesty on high, <reference osisRef="Job.26.9">Job xxvi. 9</reference>. Those that are faithful to God should endeavour likewise to appear beautiful before men, that they may <hi type="italic">adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour.</hi> [3.] For concealment. It signified the darkness of that dispensation. That which is now brought to light by the gospel, and revealed to babes, was then hidden from the wise and prudent. They saw only the coverings, not the holy things themselves (<reference osisRef="Heb.10.1">Heb. x. 1</reference>); but now Christ has <hi type="italic">destroyed the face of the covering,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.25.7">Isa. xxv. 7</reference>. (3.) When all the holy things were covered, then the Kohathites were to carry them on their shoulders. These things that had staves were carried by their staves (<reference osisRef="Num.4.6">v. 6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.4.8">8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.4.11">11,</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.4.14">14</reference>); those that had not were carried upon a bar, or bier, or bearing barrow, <reference osisRef="Num.4.10">v. 10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.4.12">12</reference>. See how the tokens of God's presence in this world are movable things; but we look for a kingdom that cannot be moved. <div eID="gen2747" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2748" type="x-p"/> 2. Eleazar, now the eldest son of Aaron, is appointed overseer of the Kohathites in this service (<reference osisRef="Num.4.16">v. 16</reference>); he must take care that nothing was forgotten, left behind, or displaced. As a priest he had more honour than the Levites, but then he had more care; and that care was a heavier burden, no doubt, upon his heart, than all the burdens that were laid upon their shoulders. It is much easier to do the work of the tabernacle than to discharge the trusts of it, to obey than to rule. <div eID="gen2748" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2749" type="x-p"/> 3. Great care must be taken to preserve the lives of these Levites, by preventing their unseasonable irreverent approach to the most holy things: <hi type="italic">Cut you not off the Kohathites,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.4.18">v. 18</reference>. Note, Those who do not what they can to keep others from sin do what they can to cut them off. [1.] The Kohathites must not see the holy things till the priests had covered them, <reference osisRef="Num.4.20">v. 20</reference>. Even those that bore the vessels of the Lord saw not what they bore, so much were even those in the dark concerning the gospel whose office it was to expound the law. And, [2.] When the holy things were covered, they might not touch them, at least not the ark, called here <hi type="italic">the holy thing,</hi> upon pain of death, <reference osisRef="Num.4.15">v. 15</reference>. Uzza was struck dead for the breach of this law. Thus were the Lord's ministers themselves then kept in fear, and that was a dispensation of terror, as well as darkness; but now, through Christ, the case is altered; we have <hi type="italic">seen with our eyes,</hi> and our <hi type="italic">hands have handles, the word of life</hi> (<reference osisRef="1John.1.1">1 John i. 1</reference>), and we are encouraged to <hi type="italic">come boldly to the throne of grace.</hi>
entries.21235d8164ae63534dd8eff1f894218efe9be075: <div eID="gen2749" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2750" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">21</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Moses, saying, <hi type="super">22</hi> Take also the sum of the sons of Gershon, throughout the houses of their fathers, by their families; <hi type="super">23</hi> From thirty years old and upward until fifty years old shalt thou number them; all that enter in to perform the service, to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. 24 This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the service of the families of the Gershonites, to serve, and for burdens: <hi type="super">25</hi> And they shall bear the curtains of the tabernacle, and the tabernacle of the congregation, his covering, and the covering of the badgers' skins that <hi type="italic">is</hi> above upon it, and the hanging for the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, <hi type="super">26</hi> And the hangings of the court, and the hanging for the door of the gate of the court, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> by the tabernacle and by the altar round about, and their cords, and all the instruments of their service, and all that is made for them: so shall they serve. <hi type="super">27</hi> At the appointment of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their burdens, and in all their service: and ye shall appoint unto them in charge all their burdens. <hi type="super">28</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the service of the families of the sons of Gershon in the tabernacle of the congregation: and their charge <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. <hi type="super">29</hi> As for the sons of Merari, thou shalt number them after their families, by the house of their fathers; <hi type="super">30</hi> From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old shalt thou number them, every one that entereth into the service, to do the work of the tabernacle of the congregation. <hi type="super">31</hi> And this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the charge of their burden, according to all their service in the tabernacle of the congregation; the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and sockets thereof, 32 And the pillars of the court round about, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords, with all their instruments, and with all their service: and by name ye shall reckon the instruments of the charge of their burden. <hi type="super">33</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the service of the families of the sons of Merari, according to all their service, in the tabernacle of the congregation, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. <div eID="gen2750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2751" type="x-p"/> We have here the charge of the other two families of the Levites, which, though not so honourable as the first, yet was necessary, and was to be done regularly. 1. The Gershonites were charged with all the drapery of the tabernacle, the curtains, and hangings, and the coverings of badgers' skins, <reference osisRef="Num.4.22-Num.4.26">v. 22-26</reference>. These they were to take down when the cloud removed, and the ark and the rest of the holy things were carried away, to pack up and bring with them, and then to set up again, where the cloud rested. Aaron and his sons allotted to them their respective charge: "You shall take care of such a curtain, and you of such a hanging, that every one may know his work, and there may be no confusion," <reference osisRef="Num.4.27">v. 27</reference>. Ithamar particularly was to take the oversight of them, <reference osisRef="Num.4.28">v. 28</reference>. 2. The Merarites were charged with the heavy carriage, the boards and bars, the pillars and sockets, the pins and cords, and these were delivered to them by name, <reference osisRef="Num.4.31-Num.4.32">v. 31, 32</reference>. An inventory was given them of every particular, that it might be forthcoming, and nothing to seek, when the tabernacle was to be set up again. Though these seemed of less importance than the other things pertaining to the sanctuary, yet there was this care taken of them, to teach us with the greatest exactness to preserve pure and entire all divine institutions, and to take care that nothing be lost. It also intimates the care God takes of his church, and every member of it; the good Shepherd <hi type="italic">calls his own sheep by name,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.10.3">John x. 3</reference>. Here were thousands of men employed about these services, though a much less number would have served for the bearing of those burdens; but it was requisite that the tabernacle should be taken down, and set up, with great expedition, and many hands would make quick work, especially when every one knew his work. They had tents of their own to take care of, and to take along with them, but the young men under thirty, and the old men above fifty, might serve for them; nor is there any mention of them, for God's house must always be preferred before our own. Their care was preposterous who built and ceiled their own houses while God's house lay waste, <reference osisRef="Hag.1.4">Hag. i. 4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hag.1.9">9</reference>. The death of the saints is represented as the taking down of the tabernacle (<reference osisRef="2Cor.5.1">2 Cor. v. 1</reference>), and the putting of it off, <reference osisRef="2Pet.1.14">2 Pet. i. 14</reference>. The immortal soul, like the most holy things, is first covered and taken away, carried by angels, unseen, under the inspection of the Lord Jesus, our Eleazar. Care is also taken of the body—the skin and flesh, which are as the curtains, the bones and sinews which are as the bars and pillars; none of these shall be lost; commandment is given concerning the bones, a covenant made with the dust; these are in safe custody, and shall all be produced in the great day, when this tabernacle shall be set up again, and these vile bodies made like the glorious body of Jesus Christ.
entries.5b0416c03e0d28e262dc7b9fe976e086656f1dd4: <div eID="gen2751" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2752" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">34</hi> And Moses and Aaron and the chief of the congregation numbered the sons of the Kohathites after their families, and after the house of their fathers, <hi type="super">35</hi> From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, every one that entereth into the service, for the work in the tabernacle of the congregation: <hi type="super">36</hi> And those that were numbered of them by their families were two thousand seven hundred and fifty. <hi type="super">37</hi> These <hi type="italic">were</hi> they that were numbered of the families of the Kohathites, all that might do service in the tabernacle of the congregation, which Moses and Aaron did number according to the commandment of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> by the hand of Moses. <hi type="super">38</hi> And those that were numbered of the sons of Gershon, throughout their families, and by the house of their fathers, <hi type="super">39</hi> From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, every one that entereth into the service, for the work in the tabernacle of the congregation, <hi type="super">40</hi> Even those that were numbered of them, throughout their families, by the house of their fathers, were two thousand and six hundred and thirty. <hi type="super">41</hi> These <hi type="italic">are</hi> they that were numbered of the families of the sons of Gershon, of all that might do service in the tabernacle of the congregation, whom Moses and Aaron did number according to the commandment of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">42</hi> And those that were numbered of the families of the sons of Merari, throughout their families, by the house of their fathers, <hi type="super">43</hi> From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, every one that entereth into the service, for the work in the tabernacle of the congregation, <hi type="super">44</hi> Even those that were numbered of them after their families, were three thousand and two hundred. 45 These <hi type="italic">be</hi> those that were numbered of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to the word of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> by the hand of Moses. <hi type="super">46</hi> All those that were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the chief of Israel numbered, after their families, and after the house of their fathers, <hi type="super">47</hi> From thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, every one that came to do the service of the ministry, and the service of the burden in the tabernacle of the congregation, <hi type="super">48</hi> Even those that were numbered of them, were eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore. <hi type="super">49</hi> According to the commandment of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> they were numbered by the hand of Moses, every one according to his service, and according to his burden: thus were they numbered of him, as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <div eID="gen2752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2753" type="x-p"/> We have here a particular account of the numbers of the three families of the Levites respectively, that is, of the effective men, between thirty years old and fifty. Observe, 1. The Kohathites were, in all, 8600 from a month old and upwards; but of these there were but 2750 serviceable men, not a third part. The Gershonites, in all, 7500, and of them but 2630 serviceable men, little more than a third part. Note, Of the many that add to the numbers of the church, there are comparatively but few that contribute to the service of it. So it has been, and so it is; many have a place in the tabernacle that do but little of the work of the tabernacle, <reference osisRef="Phil.2.20-Phil.2.21">Phil. ii. 20, 21</reference>. 2. That the Merarites were but 6200 in all, and yet of these there were 3200 serviceable men, that is, more than half. The greatest burden lay upon that family, the boards, and pillars, and sockets; and God so ordered it that, though they were the fewest in number, yet they should have the most able men among them; for whatever service God calls men to he will furnish them for it, and give strength in proportion to the work, grace sufficient. 3. The whole number of the able men of the tribe of Levi who entered into God's host to war his warfare was but 8580, whereas the able men of the other tribes that entered into the host of Israel to war their warfare were many more. The least of the tribes had almost four times as many able men as the Levites, and some of them more than eight times as many; for those that are engaged in the service of this world, and war after the flesh, are many more than those that are devoted to the service of God, and <hi type="italic">fight the good fight of faith.</hi>  <chapter eID="Num.4"/> <div eID="gen2753" type="x-p"/>

entries.8609ccc59252aebecf119fa5f544ff1cddacd57f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1261"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 4</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Num.4.1-Num.4.49">Nu 4:1-49</reference>. Of the Levites' Service.</title> <div sID="gen1713" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1261"/><hi type="bold">2-3. sons of Kohath, from thirty years old and upward--</hi>This age was specifically fixed (see on <reference osisRef="Num.8.24">Nu 8:24</reference>) as the full maturity of bodily energy to perform the laborious duties assigned them in the wilderness, as well as of mental activity to assist in the management of the sacred services. And it was the period of life at which John the Baptist and Christ entered on their respective ministries.<div eID="gen1713" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1714" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">even unto fifty--</hi>The term prescribed for active duty was a period of twenty years, at the end of which they were exempted from the physical labors of the office, though still expected to attend in the tabernacle (<reference osisRef="Num.8.26">Nu 8:26</reference>).<div eID="gen1714" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1715" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all that enter into the host--</hi>so called from their number, the order and discipline maintained through their ranks, and their special duty as guards of the tabernacle. The Hebrew word, however, signifies also a station or office; and hence the passage may be rendered, "All that enter into the sacerdotal office" (<reference osisRef="Num.4.23">Nu 4:23</reference>). <div eID="gen1715" type="x-p"/>
entries.5c011e1b7b63d3be84e53a36211fad9ceb7b0e89: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1262"/><div sID="gen1716" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1262"/><hi type="bold">4-15. This shall be the service of the sons of Kohath, &c.--</hi>They are mentioned first, from their close connection with Aaron; and the special department of duty assigned to them during the journeyings of Israel accorded with the charge they had received of the precious contents of the tabernacle. But these were to be previously covered by the common priests, who, as well as the high priest, were admitted on such necessary occasions into the holy place. This was an exception to the general rule, which prohibited the entrance of any but the high priest. But when the cloud removed from the tabernacle, the sanctuary might be entered by the common priests, as to them was reserved the exclusive privilege of packing the sacred utensils; and it was not till the holy things were thus ready for carriage, that the Kohathites were allowed to approach. <div eID="gen1716" type="x-p"/>
entries.cc61fcdc06cf8c45b6bbca03d566947d2012e828: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1270"/><div sID="gen1725" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1270"/><hi type="bold">16. to the office of Eleazar ... pertaineth the oil for the light, and the sweet incense, &c.--</hi>He was charged with the special duty of superintending the squadron who were employed in the carrying of the sacred furniture; besides, to his personal care were committed the materials requisite for the daily service, and which it was necessary he should have easily at his command (<reference osisRef="Exod.29.38">Ex 29:38</reference>). <div eID="gen1725" type="x-p"/>
entries.19521ec9b7a6c4964ed215b581c636389457b43a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1271"/><div sID="gen1726" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1271"/><hi type="bold">17-20. Cut ye not off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites, &c.--</hi>a solemn admonition to Moses and Aaron to beware, lest, by any negligence on their part, disorder and improprieties should creep in, and to take the greatest care that all the parts of this important service be apportioned to the proper parties, lest the Kohathites should be disqualified for their high and honorable duties. The guilt of their death would be incurred by the superintending priest, if he failed to give proper directions or allowed any irreverent familiarity with sacred things. <div eID="gen1726" type="x-p"/>
entries.552295f87ae920d2bca20fd682565cea455007b8: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1272"/><div sID="gen1727" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1272"/><hi type="bold">24-28. This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, &c.--</hi>They were appointed to carry "the curtains of the tabernacle"--that is, the goats' hair covering of the tent--the ten curious curtains and embroidered hangings at the entrance, with their red morocco covering, &c. <div eID="gen1727" type="x-p"/>
entries.a601c2dfe7d217962502a268a76a1d45feda1e6a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1274"/><div sID="gen1729" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1274"/><hi type="bold">29-33. As for the sons of Merari--</hi>They carried the coarser and heavier appurtenances, which, however, were so important and necessary, that an inventory was kept of them--not only on account of their number and variety, but of their comparative commonness and smallness, which might have led to their being lost or missing through carelessness, inadvertency, or neglect. It was a useful lesson, showing that God disregards nothing pertaining to His service, and that even in the least and most trivial matters, He requires the duty of faithful obedience. <div eID="gen1729" type="x-p"/>
entries.9537451c91f9baed2e7e126bc993e09820a7c7ac: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1275"/><div sID="gen1730" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1275"/><hi type="bold">34-49. Moses and Aaron and the chief of the congregation numbered the sons of the Kohathites, &c.--</hi>This enumeration was made on a different principle from that which is recorded in the preceding chapter [Nu 3:15]. That was confined to the males from a month old and upward, while this was extended to all capable of service in the three classes of the Levitical tribe. In considering their relative numbers, the wisdom of Divine Providence appears in arranging that, whereas in the Kohathites and Gershonites, whose burdens were few and easier, there were but about a third part of them which were fit for service; the Merarites, whose burdens were more and heavier, had above one half of them fit for this work [Poole]. The small population of this tribe, so inferior to that of the other tribes, is attempted to be explained (see on <reference osisRef="Num.3.39">Nu 3:39</reference>). <chapter eID="Num.4"/>

entries.642f6a59090a649edacf27b9d18c5bfb65739d77: <div eID="gen5270" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen5271" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen5272" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5272" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5271" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen5273" type="x-p"/> Moses is commanded to take the sum of the sons of Kohath from thirty years old and upward, <reference osisRef="Num.4.1-Num.4.4">Num 4:1-4</reference>. The service which they had to perform, <reference osisRef="Num.4.5-Num.4.15">Num 4:5-15</reference>. The office of Eleazar, <reference osisRef="Num.4.16">Num 4:16</reference>. The family of Kohath to be continued among the Levites, <reference osisRef="Num.4.17-Num.4.19">Num 4:17-19</reference>. They are not to go into the holy of holies, <reference osisRef="Num.4.20">Num 4:20</reference>. The sum of the sons of Gershon, <reference osisRef="Num.4.21-Num.4.23">Num 4:21-23</reference>. The service they had to perform, <reference osisRef="Num.4.24-Num.4.27">Num 4:24-27</reference>. They are to be under Ithamar, <reference osisRef="Num.4.28">Num 4:28</reference>. The sum of the sons of Merari, <reference osisRef="Num.4.29">Num 4:29</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.4.30">Num 4:30</reference>. The service they had to perform, <reference osisRef="Num.4.31-Num.4.33">Num 4:31-33</reference>. The sum of all the families of Kohath, 2,750, <reference osisRef="Num.4.34-Num.4.37">Num 4:34-37</reference>. The sum of the families of Gershon, 2,630, <reference osisRef="Num.4.38-Num.4.41">Num 4:38-41</reference>. The sum of the families of Merari, 3,200, <reference osisRef="Num.4.42-Num.4.45">Num 4:42-45</reference>. The sum total of the families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, 8,580, <reference osisRef="Num.4.46-Num.4.49">Num 4:46-49</reference>.
entries.24c881c627856a2b016e6bd78953935f4c35b1ef: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen5273" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5274" type="x-p"/> From thirty years old - In <reference osisRef="Num.8.24">Num 8:24</reference>, the Levites are ordered to enter on the service of the tabernacle at the age of twenty-five years; and in <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.24">1Chr 23:24</reference>, they were ordered to commence that work at twenty years of age. How can these different times be reconciled? <div eID="gen5274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5275" type="x-p"/> 1. At the time of which Moses speaks here, the Levitical service was exceedingly severe, and consequently required men full grown, strong, and stout, to perform it; the age therefore of thirty years was appointed as the period for commencing this service, the weightier part of which is probably here intended. <div eID="gen5275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5276" type="x-p"/> 2. In <reference osisRef="Num.8.24">Num 8:24</reference>, Moses seems to speak of the service in a general way; the severe, which was to be performed by the full-grown Levites, and the less laborious work which younger men might assist in: hence the age of twenty-five is fixed. <div eID="gen5276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5277" type="x-p"/> 3. In David's time and afterwards, in the fixed tabernacle and temple, the laboriousness of the service no longer existed, and hence twenty years was the age fixed on for all Levites to enter into the work of the sanctuary. The rabbins say that the Levites began to learn to do the service at twenty-five, and that having been instructed five years, they began the public service at thirty, and thus they reconcile the two periods referred to above. We may well suppose that the sons of the prophets continued a considerable time under instructions before they were called fully to exercise themselves in the prophetic office. <div eID="gen5277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5278" type="x-p"/> Until fifty years old - This was allowing twenty years for public severe service; a very considerate and merciful ordinance. A preacher who devotes his whole time and strength to the service of the Church of God from twenty to fifty or sixty years of age, should be then excused from his severer labor, and maintained at the charge of the sanctuary. This would not only be a great comfort to a worn-out servant of God, but also of great use to the work of the ministry, which, to be faithfully and effectually performed, requires all the powers of the body and mind of man. Old faithful ministers are to be highly respected for their work's sake, and to be supplied with all the necessaries and comforts of life; but how little can they do in the public ministry of the word, however willing to work, when their eye waxes dim and their bodily strength fails! See <reference osisRef="Num.8.25">Num 8:25</reference>. Both for their own sakes, and for the good of the Church, they should be excused from a labor to which they must be almost every way inadequate. But notwithstanding this comparative inactivity, their counsels, advice, and experience will always be considered as a treasure to the Church of Christ
entries.5e37b61ac7475c14c71ac05229951d2eb861683c: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen5278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5279" type="x-p"/> When the holy things are covered - Literally, כבלע keballa, when they are swallowed down; which shows the promptitude with which every thing belonging to the holy of holies was put out of sight, for these mysteries must ever be treated with the deepest reverence; and indeed without this they could not have been to them the representatives of heavenly realities. See the concluding note <reference osisRef="Num.4.36">Num 4:36</reference> (note).
entries.6c43eb28fdaa1a08749877e2071bd7761fa6bedd: <hi type="bold">Verse 36</hi> <div eID="gen5279" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5280" type="x-p"/> Those that were numbered - In <reference osisRef="Num.3.27">Num 3:27</reference>, etc., we have an account of the whole number of the Levites, and here of those only who were able to serve the Lord in the sanctuary. By comparing the two places we find the numbers to stand thus: - <div eID="gen5280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5281" type="x-p"/> LeviteFamily AbleMen UnableMen Total Kohathites 2,750 5,850 8,600 Gershonites 2,630 4,870 7,500 Merarites 3,200 3,000 6,200 <div eID="gen5281" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5282" type="x-p"/> Thus we find that the whole number of the Levites amounted to 22,300, of whom 3,580 were fit for service, and 13,720 unfit, being either too old or too young. What an astonishing number of men, all properly ecclesiastics; all performing some service by which God was glorified, and the congregation at large benefited! See Ainsworth. <div eID="gen5282" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5283" type="x-p"/> From this and the preceding chapter we see the very severe labor which the Levites were obliged to perform while the journeyings of the Israelites lasted. When we consider that there was not less than 10 tons 13 cwt. 24 lb. 14 oz., i. e., almost ten tons and fourteen hundred pounds' weight of metal employed in the tabernacle, (see the notes on Exodus 38 (note)), besides the immense weight of the skins, hangings, cords, boards, and posts, we shall find it was no very easy matter to transport this movable temple from place to place. <div eID="gen5283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5284" type="x-p"/> The Gershonites, who were 7,500 men in the service, had to carry the tent, coverings, veils, hangings of the court, etc., etc., <reference osisRef="Num.3.25">Num 3:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.3.26">Num 3:26</reference>. <div eID="gen5284" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5285" type="x-p"/> The Kohathites, who were 8,600 men, had to carry the ark, table, candlestick, altars, and instruments of the sanctuary, <reference osisRef="Num.3.31">Num 3:31</reference>. <div eID="gen5285" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5286" type="x-p"/> The Merarites, who were 6,200 men, had to carry the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, and all matters connected with these belonging to the tabernacle, with the pillars of the court, their sockets, pins, and cords, <reference osisRef="Num.3.36">Num 3:36</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.3.37">Num 3:37</reference>. <div eID="gen5286" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5287" type="x-p"/> The tabernacle was an epitome of the temple: the temple and tabernacle were representatives of the Church of the living God, and of the humanity of our blessed Lord. As God dwelt in the tabernacle and temple, so his fullness dwelt in the man Christ Jesus. These again were types of the Christian Church, which is termed the body of Christ, <reference osisRef="Eph.1.23">Eph 1:23</reference>, where he dwells in the plenitude of the graces of his Spirit. <div eID="gen5287" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5288" type="x-p"/> Mr. Ainsworth has a very useful note on the <reference osisRef="Num.4.20">Num 4:20</reference> verse of this chapter, the most edifying part of which I shall here lay before the reader. He considers the tabernacle and temple, not only as pointing out the old dispensation, the annulling of which was typified by their destruction, but he considers also the former as emblematical of the body of man. "The apostle," says he, "treating of the death of the saints, uses this similitude: 'If our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For we that are in This Tabernacle do groan, being burdened, not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life;' <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.1-2Cor.5.4">2Cor 5:1-4</reference>. So Peter calls his death the putting off of his Tabernacle, <reference osisRef="2Pet.1.14">2Pet 1:14</reference>. And this similitude is very fit; for, as here, in the tabernacle of Moses, <div eID="gen5288" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5289" type="x-p"/> 1. The holy things were first covered and taken away, (see <reference osisRef="Num.4.20">Num 4:20</reference>), so the soul and its powers are first withdrawn from the body by death. <div eID="gen5289" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5290" type="x-p"/> 2. As the curtains and coverings were taken off and folded up, so the skin and flesh of our bodies are pulled off and consumed. <div eID="gen5290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5291" type="x-p"/> 3. As the boards of the tabernacle were disjointed and pulled asunder, so shall our bones and sinews: compare Job's description of the formation of man, <reference osisRef="Num.10.8-Num.10.12">Num 10:8-12</reference>; and Solomon's account of his dissolution, <reference osisRef="Ecc.12.3">Ecc 12:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ecc.12.4">Ecc 12:4</reference>. <div eID="gen5291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5292" type="x-p"/> 4. As the disjointed and dissolved tabernacle was afterwards set up again, <reference osisRef="Num.10.21">Num 10:21</reference>, so shall our bodies in the day of the resurrection; see <reference osisRef="1Cor.15.51-1Cor.15.54">1Cor 15:51-54</reference>.  <chapter eID="Num.4"/> <div eID="gen5292" type="x-p"/>

entries.0158542e4260f2efb74f6e32a089120e6c5e7a7f: Num 4:1 <div eID="gen1641" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1642" type="x-p"/> Rules of Service, and Numbering of the Levites Qualified for Service. - After the adoption of the Levites for service at the sanctuary, in the place of the first-born of Israel, Moses and Aaron mustered the three families of the Levites by the command of God for the service to be performed by those who were between the ages of 30 and 50. The particulars of the service are first of all described in detail (vv. 4-33); and then the men in each family are taken, of the specified age for service (vv. 34-49). The three families are not arranged according to the relative ages of their founders, but according to the importance or sacredness of their service. The Kohathites take the lead, because the holiest parts of the tabernacle were to be carried and kept by this family, which included the priests, Aaron and his sons. The service to be performed by each of the three Levitical families is introduced in every case by a command from God to take the sum of the men from 30 years old to 50 (see Num 4:1-3, Num 4:21-23, Num 4:29 and Num 4:30).
entries.7c74805aafebe5eb2e892cdee97fb9acedad31bc: Num 4:2-3 <hi type="italic">Service of the Kohathites, and the number qualified for service</hi>. - Num 4:2, Num 4:3. “<hi type="italic">Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi:</hi>” i.e., by raising them out of the sum total of the Levites, by numbering them first and specially, viz., the men from 30 to 50 years of age, “<hi type="italic">every one who comes to the service,</hi>” i.e., who has to enter upon service “<hi type="italic">to do work at the tabernacle</hi>.” צבא (<hi type="italic">Angl</hi>. '<hi type="italic">host'</hi>) signifies military service, and is used here with special reference to the service of the Levites as the <hi type="italic">militia sacra</hi> of Jehovah.
entries.81210417e516d021fc1ce6125f40a15357f04259: Num 4:4-6 <div eID="gen1642" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1643" type="x-p"/> The service of the Kohathites at the tabernacle is (relates to) “<hi type="italic">the most holy</hi>” (see at <reference osisRef="Exod.30.10">Exo 30:10</reference>). This term includes, as is afterwards explained, the most holy things in the tabernacle, viz., the ark of the covenant, the table of shew-bread, the candlestick, the altar of incense and altar of burnt-offering, together with all the other things belonging to these. When the camp was broken up, the priests were to roll them up in wrappers, and hand them over in this state to the Kohathites, for them to carry (Num 4:5-15). First of all (Num 4:5, Num 4:6), Aaron and his sons were to take down the curtain between the holy place and the most holy (see <reference osisRef="Exod.26.31">Exo 26:31</reference>), and to cover the ark of testimony with it (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.10">Exo 25:10</reference>). Over this they were to place a wrapper of sea-cow skin (<hi type="italic">tachash</hi>, see <reference osisRef="Exod.25.5">Exo 25:5</reference>), and over this again another covering of cloth made entirely of hyacinth-coloured purple (as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.31">Exo 28:31</reference>). The sea-cow skin as to protect the inner curtain, which was covered over the ark, from storm and rain; the hyacinth purple, to distinguish the ark of the covenant as the throne of the glory of Jehovah. Lastly, they were to place the staves into the rings again, that is to say, the bearing poles, which were always left in their places on the ark (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.15">Exo 25:15</reference>), but had necessarily to be taken out while it was being covered and wrapped up.
entries.4507bfbc418f0a6a4be120618f09a0ec2802b113: Num 4:7-8 <div eID="gen1643" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1644" type="x-p"/> Over the table of shew-bread (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.23">Exo 25:23</reference>) they were to spread a hyacinth cloth, to place the plates, bowls, wine-pitchers, and drink-offering bowls (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.29">Exo 25:29</reference>) upon the top of this, and to lay shew-bread thereon; and then to spread a crimson cloth over these vessels and the shew-bread, and cover this with a sea-cow skin, and lastly to put the bearing poles in their places.
entries.f4113c4145524bce2ffaae284b843c008c4906e3: Num 4:9-10 <div eID="gen1644" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1645" type="x-p"/> The candlestick, with its lamps, snuffers, extinguishers (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.31-Exod.25.37">Exo 25:31-37</reference>), and all its oil-vessels (oil-cans), “<hi type="italic">wherewith they serve it,</hi>” i.e., prepare it for the holy service, were to be covered with a hyacinth cloth, and then with a wrapper of sea-cow skin, and laid upon the carriage. מות (Num 4:10 and Num 4:12), bearing frame, in Num 13:23 bearing poles.
entries.6bdebf0746e7556b42e2521194fe6e02be2c9ab1: Num 4:11-12 <div eID="gen1645" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1646" type="x-p"/> So again they were to wrap up the altar of incense (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.1">Exo 30:1</reference>), to adjust its bearing poles; and having wrapped it up in such coverings, along with the vessels belonging to it, to lay it upon the frame.
entries.ca6b48f9469bab30e6509397e88374de6191a70a: Num 4:13-14 <div eID="gen1646" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1647" type="x-p"/> The altar of burnt-offering was first of all to be cleansed from the ashes; a crimson cloth was then to be covered over it, and the whole of the furniture belonging to it to be placed upon the top; and lastly, the whole was to be covered with a sea-cow skin. The only thing not mentioned is the copper laver (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.18">Exo 30:18</reference>), probably because it was carried without any cover at all. The statement in the Septuagint and the Samaritan text, which follows Num 4:14. respecting its covering and conveyance upon a frame, is no doubt a spurious interpolation.
entries.48ddde9a0de11f92fe16cdb4acba6a7f58227ea6: Num 4:15 <div eID="gen1647" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1648" type="x-p"/> After the priests had completed the wrapping up of all these things, the Kohathites were to come up to carry them; but they were not to touch “the holy” (the holy things), lest they should die (see Num 1:53; Num 18:3, and comp. <reference osisRef="2Sam.6.6-2Sam.6.7">2Sa 6:6-7</reference>).
entries.91a40ed7e05c58d17ae9573dabb795baff8d23bb: Num 4:16 <div eID="gen1648" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1649" type="x-p"/> The oversight of the oil for the candlestick (<reference osisRef="Exod.27.20">Exo 27:20</reference>), the incense (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.34">Exo 30:34</reference>), the continual meat-offering (<reference osisRef="Exod.29.40">Exo 29:40</reference>), and the anointing oil (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.23">Exo 30:23</reference>), belonged to Eleazar as the head of all the Levites (Num 3:32). He had also the oversight of the dwelling and all the holy things and furniture belonging to it; and, as a comparison of Num 4:28 and Num 4:33 clearly shows, of the services of the Kohathites also.
entries.d3776b48913c60c1fa6196676c2334fd5faee324: Num 4:17-18 <div eID="gen1649" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1650" type="x-p"/> In order to prevent as far as possible any calamity from befalling the Levites while carrying the most holy things, the priests are again urged by the command of God to do what has already been described in detail in Num 4:5-15, lest through any carelessness on their part they should cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites, i.e., should cause their destruction; viz., if they should approach the holy things before they had been wrapped up by Aaron and his sons in the manner prescribed and handed over to them to carry. If the Kohathites should come for only a single moment to look at the holy things, they would die. אל־תּכריתוּ, “<hi type="italic">cut ye not off,</hi>” i.e., “take care that the Kohathites are not cut off through your mistake and negligence” (<hi type="italic">Ros</hi>.). “<hi type="italic">The tribe of the families of the Kohathites:</hi>” <hi type="italic">shebet</hi>, the tribe, is not used here, as it frequently is, in its derivative sense of tribe (<hi type="italic">Tribus</hi>), but in the original literal sense of <hi type="italic">stirps</hi>.
entries.6f17b77cc5133c8c285b7e22576d3c8225606a74: Num 4:19 <div eID="gen1650" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1651" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">This do to them:</hi>” sc., what is prescribed in Num 4:5-15 with reference to their service.
entries.76fe6227ea8d7fb0f3dd945df39e6c2719455f8c: Num 4:20 כּבלּע, “<hi type="italic">like a swallow, a gulp,</hi>” is probably a proverbial expression, according to the analogy of <reference osisRef="Job.7.19">Job 7:19</reference>, for “<hi type="italic">a single instant,</hi>” of which the Arabic also furnishes examples (see <hi type="italic">A. Schultens</hi> on <reference osisRef="Job.7.19">Job 7:19</reference>). The <hi type="italic">Sept</hi>. rendering, ἐξάπινα, conveys the actual sense. A historical illustration of Num 4:20 is furnished by 1Sa 6:19.<note placement="foot">According to <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>, Num 4:17-20 have been interpolated by the Jehovist into the Elohistic text. But the reasons for this assumption are weak throughout. Neither the peculiar use of the word shebet, to which there is no corresponding parallel in the whole of the Old Testament, nor the construction of נגשׁ with את, which is only met with in <reference osisRef="1Sam.9.18">1Sa 9:18</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Sam.30.21">1Sa 30:21</reference>, nor the <hi type="italic">Hiphil</hi> הכרית, can be regarded as criteria of a Jehovistic usage. And the assertion, that the Elohist lays the emphasis upon approaching and touching the holy things (Num 4:15; Num 8:19; Num 18:3, Num 18:22), and not upon seeing or looking at them, rests upon an antithesis which is arbitrarily forced upon the text, since not only seeing (Num 4:20), but touching also (Num 4:19), is described as causing death; so that seeing and touching form no antithesis at all.</note>
entries.4563b35ce75fccee7c54bfe31f026e8c03c4d5a1: Num 4:21-26 <hi type="italic">The service of the Gershonites</hi> is introduced in Num 4:21-23 in the same manner as that of the Kohathites in Num 4:1-3; and in Num 4:24-26 it is described in accordance with the brief notice and explanation already given in Num 3:24-26.
entries.0a8e151f20b5264470c0a1583031c8985605a112: Num 4:27 <div eID="gen1651" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1652" type="x-p"/> Their service was to be performed “<hi type="italic">according to the mouth</hi> (i.e., according to the appointment) <hi type="italic">of Aaron and his sons, with regard to all their carrying</hi> (all that they were to carry), <hi type="italic">and all their doing</hi>.” - “<hi type="italic">And ye </hi>(the priests) <hi type="italic">shall appoint to them for attendance</hi> (in charge) <hi type="italic">all their carrying</hi>,” i.e., all the things they were to carry. בּמשׁמרת פּקד, to give into keeping. The combination of פּקד with בּ and the accusative of the object is analogous to בּ נתן, to give into a persons’ hand, in <reference osisRef="Gen.27.17">Gen 27:17</reference>; and there is no satisfactory reason for any such emendations of the text as <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> proposes.

entries.f6515f7eb4ad6d362b4b52730578459dec1f9f3d: Num 4:34-48 <div eID="gen1654" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1655" type="x-p"/> Completion of the prescribed mustering, and statement of the number of men qualified for service in the three Levitical families: viz., 2750 Kohathites, 2630 Gershonites, and 3200 Merarites - in all, 8580 Levites fit for service: a number which bears a just proportion to the total number of male Levites of a month old and upwards, viz., 22,000.
entries.0d5748a309582d95e6dd7e1da72bb21366682aba: Num 4:49 <div eID="gen1655" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1656" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">According to the commandment of Jehovah, they appointed them through the hand of Moses</hi> (i.e., under his direction), <hi type="italic">each one to his service, and his burden, and his mustered things</hi> (פּקדיו), i.e., the things assigned to him at the time of the mustering as his special charge (see <reference osisRef="Exod.38.21">Exo 38:21</reference>). Spiritual Organization of the <div eID="gen1656" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1657" type="x-p"/> Congregation of Israel - Numbers 5-6 <div eID="gen1657" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1658" type="x-p"/> From the outward organization of the tribes of Israel as the army of Jehovah, the law proceeds to their internal moral and spiritual order, for the purpose of giving an  inward support, both moral and religious, to their outward or social and political unity. This is the object of the directions concerning the removal of unclean persons from the camp (Num 5:1-4), the restitution of anything unjustly appropriated (Num 5:5-10), the course to be pursued with a wife suspected of adultery (Num 5:11-31), and also of the laws relating to the Nazarite (Num 6:1-21), and to the priestly blessing (Num 6:22-27).  <chapter eID="Num.4"/> <div eID="gen1658" type="x-p"/>

entries.c48af9c11f885c9477abc8aa076d58d6fd75869c: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.4.1" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.4.1" sID="gen18784" type="section"/> <div sID="gen18785" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1. </hi><hi type="italic">And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron</hi> This <hi type="italic">census</hi> had a different object from the former one, which we have just been considering, viz., that an equal distribution of the charges should be made in proportion to the number of the individuals. First, as regarded age, a distinction must be observed between this tribe and the others; for we have already seen that all the Israelites above twenty years of age were numbered, because they were then fit to bear arms. But it was not without reason that a more mature age was required in the case of the Levites, so that they should not begin to discharge their ministry before their thirtieth year. For not only is strength and rigor of body requisite for spiritual warfare, but seriousness and gravity also. If they had been admitted in their youth, their levity might have detracted from the reverence due to sacred things, since the young are often led to act intemperately by their fervor and licentiousness. Access to the sanctuary, therefore, was not permitted them till they had grown up to be men; for by their thirtieth year men ought to have become so staid, as that it shall be base and inexcusable for them to give way to the wantonness of youth.<div eID="gen18785" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18786" type="x-p"/>From their fiftieth year they were released from their duties; since sloth and inactivity generally accompany old age. The case is different as to war, because we find many who are vigorous after their fiftieth year. Furthermore, since religion is more precious than all earthly affairs, diligent care was to be taken lest it should fall into disesteem on account of the idleness and somnolency of its ministers.<div eID="gen18786" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.4.1" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen18784" osisID="Num.4.1" type="section"/>
entries.fdd8dc529dfcff7ff8f46490b8e8f4321f6dfafc: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.4.4" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.4.4" sID="gen12177" type="section"/> <div sID="gen12178" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4.</hi> <hi type="italic">This shall be the service of the sons of Kohath.</hi> He assigns their various offices to the Levites: firstly, lest their promiscuous sedulity should beget confusion; secondly, lest ambition should stimulate certain of them, <note n="203"> <div sID="gen12179" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">D’ s’avancer, ou ingerer</foreign>:” to put themselves forward, or to interfere. — <hi type="italic">Fr.</hi><div eID="gen12179" type="x-p"/> </note> from whence disputes and contentions might arise. We know how confusedly men work unless a certain rule is prescribed to them, lest they should run about in an aimless hurry; and whilst each individual desires to anticipate others, an unworthy emulation ensues, which afterwards vents itself in quarrels. If, therefore, this had not been prevented, the Levites would soon have made disturbances in their duty, and contentions would have taken place between them. God, then, comes forward, and by His own authority confines them all within their proper bounds, and restrains their foolish passions. That a more honorable office is assigned to the sons of Kohath than to the others, proceeds from God’s gratuitous favor; and thus all pride was suppressed, lest any should boast of his dexterity, or industry, or other gifts. The charge of the Holy of holies is, therefore, entrusted to the sons of Kohath; not that they should handle any part of it, but only that they should carry on the march its vessels, when packed by the priests; for God commands the sons of Aaron to come and take down the sanctuary, and carefully cover the veil, the altar, and other sacred vessels with their proper covers, before the sons of Kohath laid a finger upon them, that thus the reverence of the people for holy things might be increased; and besides, that when the other tribes should see even the Levites forbidden from touching the sanctuary, they might be reminded of their unworthiness and humbled the more. Moreover, all cause of envy was removed when the other Levites heard that a perilous duty was entrusted to the sons of Kohath, for God threatens them with death if they touch any forbidden thing: and lastly, admonishes the priests, the sons of Aaron, lest by their carelessness they should destroy their brethren; for, if they should leave anything uncovered, they would be the cause of their destruction.<div eID="gen12178" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.4.4" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen12177" osisID="Num.4.4" type="section"/>

The tasks which He enjoins upon the sons of Gershon, as well as the sons of Merari, are apparently mean and laborious, for it was a hard and also a servile work to carry the curtains and the tabernacle, together with its coverings, the boards, too, and the bars, and the pillars.
